#### Import packages

Import the different libraries we will need.

```{r, message=FALSE}
library("tidyverse")
library("curl")
```

#### Load data

Import the data from Kaggle ("https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/piotrgrabo/breastcancerproteomes?select=77_cancer_proteomes_CPTAC_itraq.csv")

```{r}
# Create data folders
dir.create("../data/_raw", recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

# Download data
curl_download(
  url = "https://www.kaggle.com/api/v1/datasets/download/piotrgrabo/breastcancerproteomes",
  destfile = "../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip",
  mode = "wb"
)

# Unzip
unzip("../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip",
      exdir = "../data/_raw")

# Remove ZIP archive
invisible(file.remove("../data/_raw/breastcancerproteomes.zip"))
```

```{r, warning=FALSE}
# Load datasets into environment
file_names <- c(
  "77_cancer_proteomes_CPTAC_itraq.csv",
  "clinical_data_breast_cancer.csv",
  "PAM50_proteins.csv"
)

proteomes <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[1]), show_col_types = FALSE)
clinical  <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[2]), show_col_types = FALSE)
pam50     <- read_csv(str_c("../data/_raw/", file_names[3]), show_col_types = FALSE)
```

### Correlation between duplicates

First we check the correlation between duplicated to be sure that that duplicates from the same patient are consistent. 

```{r}
sample_cols  <- str_subset(names(proteomes), "TCGA")
patients     <- str_split_i(sample_cols, "[_|.]", 1)
dup_patients <- unique(patients[duplicated(patients)])

dup_cor_matrices <- map(dup_patients, \(p) {
  proteomes |>
    select(all_of(sample_cols[patients == p])) |>
    cor(use = "pairwise.complete.obs") |>
    round(3)
}) |>
  set_names(dup_patients)

dup_cor_matrices
```

### Mean the duplicates and renaming

Then we merge those duplicated so that each patient has only one measurement. 
Consequently, patients having more than one sample will have a single value per protein (equal to the average of their replicates).
Two versions of the dataset are created:
- including the healthy control samples
- only with tumor samples

```{r}
proteomes_mean_with_control <- proteomes |>
  # 1. Long format: all sample columns (everything except the 3 annotation columns)
  pivot_longer(cols = -c(RefSeq_accession_number, gene_symbol, gene_name),
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "log2_ratio") |>
  # 2. Patient ID: tumors get TCGA-AO-A12D format, controls keep their own name
  mutate(patient_id = if_else(str_detect(sample, "TCGA"),
                              str_c("TCGA-", str_split_i(sample, "[_|.]", 1)),
                              sample)) |>
  # 3. Mean per protein and patient (only the replicates actually change)
  group_by(RefSeq_accession_number, gene_symbol, gene_name, patient_id) |>
  summarise(log2_ratio = mean(log2_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  # 4. NaN (both copies missing) -> NA
  mutate(log2_ratio = if_else(is.nan(log2_ratio), NA_real_, log2_ratio)) |>
  # 5. Back to wide format
  pivot_wider(names_from = patient_id,
              values_from = log2_ratio)
```

```{r}
proteomes_mean_without_control <- proteomes |>
  # 1. Long format: one row per protein and sample
  pivot_longer(cols = contains("TCGA"),
               names_to = "sample",
               values_to = "log2_ratio") |>
  # 2. Patient ID from the sample name: AO-A12D.01TCGA -> TCGA-AO-A12D
  mutate(patient_id = str_c("TCGA-", str_split_i(sample, "[_|.]", 1))) |>
  # 3. Mean per protein and patient (replicates are averaged, others are unchanged)
  group_by(RefSeq_accession_number, gene_symbol, gene_name, patient_id) |>
  summarise(log2_ratio = mean(log2_ratio, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  # 4. If both copies are missing, mean() gives NaN; make it a normal NA
  mutate(log2_ratio = if_else(is.nan(log2_ratio), NA_real_, log2_ratio)) |>
  # 5. Back to wide format: one column per patient
  pivot_wider(names_from = patient_id,
              values_from = log2_ratio)
```

### Renaming columns of the PAM50 file before mergeing

Look at the pam50 dataset

```{r}
head(pam50)
```
Before filtering the proteomic dataset with the PAM50 reference list, we rename RefSeqProteinID to RefSeq_accession_number in the pam50 table so that both of the dataset have the same key column name for joining. 

```{r}
pam50 <- pam50 |> 
  rename(RefSeq_accession_number = RefSeqProteinID)
```


### Merge data

#### Merge the PAM50 dataset with the proteomes dataset

The PAM50 dataset contains the relevant proteins to study for the different subtypes of breast cancer. Consequently, we merge those two dataset to keep only the relevant proteins in our study.
Merging at the time of the study is interesting because the results will be much sharper and easier to interpret.

```{r}
# left joins to only keep the 100 reference genes for breast cancer
proteomes_with_control_pam50_joined <-  inner_join(pam50,proteomes_mean_with_control, 
                                                   by ="RefSeq_accession_number")

proteomes_without_control_pam50_joined <- inner_join(pam50,proteomes_mean_without_control, 
                                                      by = "RefSeq_accession_number")

head(proteomes_with_control_pam50_joined)
head(proteomes_without_control_pam50_joined)
```

This first step merged the two tables according to the RefSeq_accession_number column. 

### Merge the filtered proteomes dataset with the clinical dataset

Here is a visualization of the clinical metadata

```{r}
head(clinical)
```
Before merging those two tables, we need to be sure that they share a common structure and that patients ID match. 

First, we need to pivot the proteomes dataset so patients will be on rows as for the clinical table and unique protein isoforms on columns.
Use the proteomes without control because we are only interested into tumors and not the healthy data. 

```{r}
proteomes_without_control_transposed <- proteomes_without_control_pam50_joined |> 
  # create an unique ID for each isoform 
  mutate(protein_id = str_c(gene_symbol, "_", RefSeq_accession_number)) |> 
  # keep only the new ID and patients columns 
  select(protein_id, starts_with("TCGA")) |>  
  # put each patient on one row 
  pivot_longer(
    # take all the columns from the patients (= everything but proteins_id)
    cols = -protein_id, 
    names_to = "patient_id",
    # log 
    values_to = "log2_ratio"
  ) |> 
  # put each unique protein as an unique column  
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = protein_id,
    values_from = log2_ratio
  )

head(proteomes_without_control_transposed)
```
We went from proteome filtered datset where patients are in columns and lines are proteins.
We took all the columns of the patients and tranformed it in lines containing each patient + protein + value associated (pivot_longer step).
And after take all the proteins and spread them into columns (pivot_wider step).
=> the same structure than the clinical table.  

Now, the objective is to merge the clinical metadata to add relevant informations to the filtered proteomes dataset.

```{r}
final_without_control_dataset <- inner_join(proteomes_without_control_transposed, clinical, 
                            by = c("patient_id" = "Complete TCGA ID")
)

View(final_without_control_dataset)
```


```{r}
proteomes_with_control_transposed <- proteomes_with_control_pam50_joined |> 
  # create an unique ID for each isoform 
  mutate(protein_id = str_c(gene_symbol, "_", RefSeq_accession_number)) |> 
  # keep only the new ID and patients columns 
  select(protein_id, ends_with("CPTAC") | starts_with("TCGA")) |> 
  # put each patient on one row 
  pivot_longer(
    # take all the columns from the patients (= everything but proteins_id)
    cols = -protein_id, 
    names_to = "patient_id",
    # log 
    values_to = "log2_ratio"
  ) |> 
  # put each unique protein as an unique column  
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = protein_id,
    values_from = log2_ratio
  )

head(proteomes_with_control_transposed)
```

```{r}
final_with_control_dataset <- left_join(
  proteomes_with_control_transposed, 
  clinical, 
  by = c("patient_id" = "Complete TCGA ID")
)

View(final_with_control_dataset)
```
